subject: HIPAA BAA availability & PHI handling — deployment suitability recap
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardioworks.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: HIPAA / BAA conversation & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of the call
- CardioWorks use case: real-time ECG feature extraction + downstream analytics. You indicated patient-level identifiers and raw ECG traces will be part of the data sent to the model pipeline.
- Primary ask: confirm whether Redwood can enter a BAA and which deployment modes are eligible for PHI.

High-level guidance (from our product/security side)
- Hosted API (Redwood Hosted): NOT suitable for PHI by default. We can discuss carve-outs, but standard hosted endpoints do not meet our PHI handling policy because of multi-tenant control plane and accessible persistent telemetry.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity + VPC peering): ELIGIBLE when paired with a signed BAA, VPC/private networking, and customer-managed KMS; requires configuration review.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): RECOMMENDED for regulated workloads that want full isolation — eligible and the most straightforward path for strict PHI requirements.

Clarifying questions for you (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the exact PHI elements you expect to send? (examples: name, MRN, SSN, DOB, raw ECG waveform).
2) Do you need embeddings or model outputs persisted on our side? If yes, what retention window is required?
3) Do you have a preference between Dedicated vs. Private from an operations perspective?

Attachments & artifacts
- Attached: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (summary of our SOC 2 posture).
- I can send our standard BAA template immediately on request (we prefer to iterate, not delay).

Proposed next steps
- Alex to share vendor security questionnaire and confirm PHI scope (you mentioned procurement will join).
- We (security + engineering) to review the questionnaire and produce a HIPAA deployment matrix for the three hosting options.
- Schedule a 30-min security deep-dive with your infra/security team and our Security Engineer (Rishi). I propose Tue/Wed next week.

If the above aligns, I’ll queue the BAA template and ask Rishi to draft the deployment matrix so you have a concise playbook.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Thanks Ava — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from CardioWorks: 

PHI scope
- We will be sending patient identifiers (first/last name, MRN), DOB, and full ECG waveform data (no SSNs). We will also attach a patient pseudonym in some payloads.
- We expect to persist embeddings for analytics and cohorting for approximately 30 days.

Questionnaire & timeline
- Attached is our Vendor Security Questionnaire (CardioWorks_Vendor_Sec_Q.pdf). Procurement wants to get visibility into SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, key management, logging/audit retention, and BAA availability.
- Our procurement team prefers Dedicated with VPC if Redwood supports the same guarantees you discussed. If not, we’ll evaluate Private deployment.

Immediate asks
1) Please send the BAA template for our legal team review.
2) Confirm whether Dedicated + VPC supports customer-managed KMS and whether logs/audit can be retained for 1 year (we may need longer for compliance).
3) Any short notes on how Redwood prevents accidental cache persistence of PHI (KV cache behavior).

Thanks — Alex

Alex Moreno
Head of IT Security | CardioWorks
alex.moreno@cardioworks.com
Attachment: CardioWorks_Vendor_Sec_Q.pdf (application/pdf, 1.1 MB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardioworks.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: HIPAA / BAA conversation & next steps

Alex — thanks for the questionnaire and the PHI clarification. Quick technical assessment and proposed controls below. Replying All so procurement/security can see the plan.

Short answers to your asks
- BAA: we can provide our BAA template (Ava will send). We can enter a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted (multi-tenant public endpoints) is not supported for PHI in our standard offering.
- Dedicated + VPC: supports customer-managed KMS. We can configure TLS + mTLS for service endpoints and peering. Audit logs can be exported into your logging project; retention is configurable but will need a scoped SLA — 1 year is possible with the dedicated retention add-on.
- KV cache & accidental persistence: runtime uses ephemeral KV caches per-process; by default we do not persist model KV caches to durable storage. For PHI workloads we can enable strict in-memory-only mode and disable telemetry collection of prompt/response text. We recommend also enabling prefix redaction/tokenization at the client side for additional safety.

Action items (internal & external)
1) Alex / CardioWorks: confirm final PHI element list and retention requirement for embeddings (30 days noted).
2) Ava: share BAA template and the SOC2 summary (Ava already attached).
3) Security (Rishi) + Prod Infra: produce a 1‑page HIPAA deployment matrix that maps PHI types -> eligible deployment modes -> required controls. I’ll draft and attach as hipaa_deploy_matrix.csv for your review.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with CardioWorks infra + Redwood Security (Rishi) next week. Ava, please coordinate calendar.

Notes/risks
- If CardioWorks requires embedding permanence beyond 90 days and wants hosted convenience, we will need legal and infra exceptions; we should avoid that path where possible.
- QSA involvement: if CardioWorks wants an external QSA assessment or a managed onboarding for Private, we’ll coordinate through our Compliance partner.

Draft attachment: hipaa_deploy_matrix.csv (see attached stub)
